text: A teacher reads your surname off the register and sighs. 'I taught the last one of you. And the one before.'

right.label: Live it down
right.result: By Friday the sigh has a new reason.

risk.result: Everyone now expects it of you.

text: 'Your family has always done well,' says the careers teacher, looking at your marks. 'Until now.'

right.label: Break the chain
right.result: Somebody had to. You feel almost historic.

risk.result: The pressure is something else.

text: The portrait of the one who left you everything hangs in the hall. The eyes follow you. So does the disappointment.

left.label: Take it down
left.result: It leaves a pale square on the wall. The square also judges you.

right.label: Leave it up
right.result: You nod at it every morning. It has not nodded back.

up.label: Hang a second one next to it

risk.result: Two sets of eyes now.

text: You find the family watch in a drawer. It stopped the minute its last owner did. A dealer offers $4,000.

left.label: Sell it
left.result: The dealer sells it on for nine. You learn this at a bad moment.

right.label: Wear it
right.result: It is never right. You are late for everything, with dignity.

up.label: Wind it and wear it for life

risk.result: It gets stuck on a Tuesday.

text: A cousin you have never met says the will was wrong and they want their share. They have brought a folder.

risk.result: It was a very good folder.

right.label: Pay them off
right.result: They send a Christmas card every year now. It always mentions the folder.

up.label: Meet them and hear their story

risk.result: The story goes on a while.

text: The family plot at the cemetery has one space left. The office rings to ask if you'd like to reserve it.

left.label: Reserve it
left.result: Your name is on a list. It is the one waiting list you are in no hurry on.

right.label: Hang up
right.result: They ring again next year. They are patient people.

up.label: Book a plot for each of the family

risk.result: The office also offers a payment plan.

text: Every year your family eats the same grey pudding on the same day. Nobody likes it. This year it is your turn to make it.

left.label: Make it
left.result: It is as bad as ever. Everyone is delighted.

right.label: Order pizza
right.result: Your aunt does not speak to you until spring.

up.label: Cook it for the whole village

risk.result: Forty bowls of grey pudding.

text: On an old door frame you find a parent's height marks in pencil, year by year. At your age they were taller.

right.label: Add your mark
right.result: You stand very straight. It doesn't help.

risk.result: The landlord isn't thrilled.

text: An old neighbour tells you your family is cursed: not one of you has ever died peacefully. They say it kindly.

risk.result: You trip on their step on the way out. Coincidence.

right.label: See a priest
right.result: The priest says it's nonsense, then blesses you twice to be safe.

up.label: Hire an expert to lift it

risk.result: The expert is a bit of a fraud.

text: In the attic: a letter marked 'to be opened when I am gone'. It is mostly about the boiler.

left.label: Read on

risk.result: There was a catch.

left.result: The last line is about you. It is better than the boiler part.

right.label: Put it back
right.result: You still don't know how the boiler works.

up.label: Read it aloud at the family dinner

risk.result: There's a second page about the boiler.

text: A relative has heard you came into money. They have a business idea. It involves alpacas.

left.label: Invest
left.result: You own a share of eleven alpacas.

risk.result: Alpacas, it turns out, are in.

right.label: Decline
right.result: They tell the whole family you've changed.

risk.result: The alpacas escape.

text: A website offers to trace your family tree for $200.

risk.result: Seven generations of people who died of things you also have.
The tree has an awkward branch.

text: Family reunion. Forty relatives, one barbecue, and an uncle with opinions.

left.label: Go
left.result: You are told you look tired by nine separate people.

risk.result: Nobody leaves before Tuesday.

text: A man at a market stall sells you your family crest. It has a lion on it. Nobody in your family has ever met a lion.

left.label: Buy it
left.result: It goes above the toilet. The lion looks unsure.

up.label: Put it on everything you own

risk.result: People ask why you own a lion.

text: A local historian wants to write a book about your family. They ask if there's anything you'd like left out.

left.label: Tell all
left.result: Chapter six ends two friendships and one marriage. Not yours.

right.label: Leave things out
right.result: The book is short and very polite.

risk.result: One diary is quite spicy.

text: The council offers a memorial bench with your family name on it for $900. You are not dead, but they suggest planning ahead.

left.label: Buy it
left.result: You sit on it most days. Checking the quality.

up.label: Buy a bench for every park

risk.result: The council bills you for a plaque.
